value_hypothesis.beneficiary: Users who reported trouble and modified or interrupted retinoid use; concentration, prior exposure, skin context and benefit targets need alignment.
value_hypothesis.incremental_gain: Investigate whether an available beginner-oriented product/routine already permits the desired retinoid-related use without the observed self-adjustment or interruption. A new product is not yet justified.
value_hypothesis.uncertainties: Two source-local users are not a validated target segment. Product strength/identity, causation, clinical severity, recovery cost/duration, efficacy and adequacy of existing milder or blended products are unknown. This is no dosing or mixing advice.
value_hypothesis.falsifier: Stop the new-product premise if a suitable existing product or ordinary accepted routine solves the same user/context requirements. Hold if the two reports cannot support a coherent comparable requirement.

value_hypothesis.beneficiary: Users reporting opposite filter-class switches with remaining discomfort; exact products, contexts and desired protection requirements need matching.
value_hypothesis.incremental_gain: Investigate whether an available sunscreen already meets the same eye-comfort and daytime skin-comfort requirements. The value hypothesis is sustaining acceptable use, not inventing a universal filter-class solution.
value_hypothesis.uncertainties: Self-reported symptoms do not diagnose sensitive skin or implicate filters. Different individual problems may not support one common requirement. Available mineral/mixed products may fully solve them; no efficacy or SPF measurement is available.
